install_tell: git clone https://github.com/lightdash/lightdash && cd lightdash && cp .env.development.local.example .env && docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up (publishes ${PORT:-8080}:${PORT:-8080}); production self-host requires LIGHTDASH_SECRET, SITE_URL, PGCONNECTIONURI set
misconfig_patterns: Pre-setup race: a fresh instance with zero orgs returns health.results.requiresOrgRegistration=true; the first visitor to /register creates the organization and becomes its admin. Internet-exposed un-set-up instance = claimable admin (read-only confirm via /api/v1/health, no register POST).
LIGHTDASH_SECRET copied from .env.development ('not very secret') into production => known token-signing secret; session/token forgery surface. Operators who lift the dev env file inherit it.
SECURE_COOKIES=false + TRUST_PROXY=false (dev defaults) behind an HTTPS reverse proxy => session cookie not flagged Secure; docs explicitly say flip both to true in prod.
ALLOW_MULTIPLE_ORGS=true lets any registrant spin up their own org on a shared instance (separate-tenant self-registration); default false keeps the instance invite-only after first org exists.

No whole-app unauth mode exists. Unlike Superset (admin/admin) or Redash, every data/AI path is behind a session by default => high-depth low-breadth posture; the only standing open door is the pre-setup window.

response_markers: JSON results.version = real instance version (not in HTML)
JSON results.isAuthenticated=false for an anonymous probe (first-class field)
active_probe.false_positive_check: The word 'Lightdash' appears on www.lightdash.com and doc/blog mirrors and on dashboards a user titled 'Lightdash' inside another BI tool. To avoid the ~50% title-only false positive, confirm the unauth JSON contract: GET /api/v1/health must return HTTP 200 with a JSON object whose results carry BOTH a `version` string AND a `requiresOrgRegistration` key AND `auth.disablePasswordAuthentication`. No other product emits that field set; a marketing page or doc mirror 404s the route. Distinguish a claimable-admin pre-setup instance (results.requiresOrgRegistration=true) from a normal locked instance (false, isAuthenticated=false, data routes 401). Surface fingerprinted != access exercised: /health open does NOT mean data is open; /api/v1/org returning 401/403 confirms the session gate holds.

deployment_tells: Backend listens on PORT=8080; docker-compose publishes ${PORT:-8080}:${PORT:-8080}; almost always reverse-proxied to 80/443 with a hostname
GET /api/v1/health = near-zero-cost unauth liveness + identity + state + AI-wired + attribution in one blob
Sidecar ports: PGPORT 5432 (metadata Postgres, not the warehouse), HEADLESS_BROWSER_PORT 3000 (export puppeteer), LIGHTDASH_PROMETHEUS_PORT 9090 (off by default)
Session cookie connect.sid (express-session default; CANDIDATE, may be overridden)
pivot_paths: Read /api/v1/health unauth for version (CVE scoping), claimable-admin state (requiresOrgRegistration), AI-on (ai.isAmbientAiEnabled), warehouse class (auth.snowflake/databricks.enabled), and operator hostname (siteUrl) - all pre-auth, read-only
If requiresOrgRegistration=true: instance is un-set-up; the next /register creates org admin. CONFIRM read-only via health only; do NOT POST /register against survey hosts (names ARE the finding)
Cert-CN attribution sweep ssl.cert.subject.cn:lightdash for operator self-host clusters

Post-auth (out of recon scope): AI agents answer over dbt semantic layer + warehouse; MCP server (Claude/Cursor) gives write access to the analytics layer; CVE-2024-6585 XSS / CVE-2024-6586 SSRF need editor/admin
vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-6585 / GHSA-6529-6jv3-66q2 - stored XSS in markdown dashboards + dashboard comments (High, CVSS 8.7); auth required (Admin/Editor); affects 0.1024.6; fixed 0.1042.2
CVE-2024-6586 / GHSA-4h7x-6vxh-7hjf - SSRF session-takeover via dashboard export, exporting user leaks session token (High, CVSS 7.3); auth required; affects 0.1024.6; fixed 0.1027.2

No pre-auth RCE / authz-bypass CVE found. Primary misconfig class is non-CVE: requiresOrgRegistration=true claimable-admin pre-setup window + copied dev LIGHTDASH_SECRET + SECURE_COOKIES=false behind a proxy
auth_evidence: PRIMARY SOURCE: HealthService.ts sets `const isAuthenticated = !!user?.userUuid` and `const requiresOrgRegistration = !(await this.organizationModel.hasOrgs())`; an anonymous probe is a first-class case (isAuthenticated:false) on a 200 /api/v1/health, but every data/project/AI route sits behind the session. .env.development ships AUTH_DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTHENTICATION=false (password login on) and all OIDC providers enabled:false. There is NO ALLOW_SELF_REGISTRATION flag and NO whole-app unauth mode. Registration = first-user-claims-org-admin, then invite-only (ALLOW_MULTIPLE_ORGS=false default). Therefore Lightdash is auth-mandatory-multiuser: data is never default-open; the only standing exposure is a transient un-set-up instance. This CONFIRMS Insight #40 (auth-on-default shifts rightward in newer OSS): Lightdash is materially more locked down than Superset (admin/admin) or Redash.
sensitive_assets: (pre-auth, via /api/v1/health) instance version, claimable-admin state, AI-agents-enabled flag, warehouse class, operator hostname (siteUrl)

(post-auth, out of recon scope) dbt semantic-layer model + metric definitions, project/warehouse connection config, chart/dashboard data over BigQuery/Snowflake/Postgres/Databricks, AI agent prompts/threads, warehouse credentials, embedded-analytics secrets, MCP write surface
